sports.nri_angle: The World Cup Round of 32 match was played at Levi’s Stadium in Santa Clara — the heart of Silicon Valley — making it a once-in-a-generation live sporting event for Bay Area NRIs, many of whom have adopted American soccer as a second sporting passion.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: Tielemans in the 125th Minute. Belgium Came Back From the Dead in Seattle — and NRIs in the Pacific Northwest Had Front-Row Seats.

sports.image_caption: Youri Tielemans in Belgium colors during the March 2026 friendly against the United States
sports.nri_angle: Seattle's 100,000+ Indian tech community had front-row seats to the World Cup's most dramatic comeback — and Belgium's Round of 16 match is also at Lumen Field, keeping the tournament in the Pacific Northwest NRI heartland.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.image_caption: Harry Kane in action for England — the Bayern Munich striker now has 13 World Cup goals
sports.nri_angle: With the World Cup on American soil, millions of NRIs are watching history unfold in their own cities — from Kane's record-breaking night in Atlanta to tonight's USA match in the Bay Area.

sports.nri_angle: The IPL trade window has become appointment viewing for NRI fans worldwide — Pandya's move will reshape the league that connects the diaspora to Indian cricket year-round.

sports.title: The World Cup Bracket Is Set — and It’s Coming to Your Neighborhood

sports.nri_angle: Round of 16 venues — Houston, MetLife (NJ), Philadelphia, Seattle, Atlanta, Arlington, Vancouver — map almost perfectly onto the largest Indian-American population centers. For millions of NRIs, this is the first World Cup they can attend in person.

sports.image_caption: Ishan Kishan, India's new No.1 ranked T20I batter, has completed a remarkable rise from a mental health break to the top of the world rankings.
sports.nri_angle: Indian batter reaching world No.1 in T20I rankings ahead of a series on English soil is a point of pride for NRI cricket fans. Kishan's comeback from mental health challenges resonates with diaspora themes of resilience and reinvention.

sports.title: Ashwin in America. Cricket Has Never Had This Kind of Star Power on U.S. Soil.

sports.image_caption: Ravichandran Ashwin in bowling action during a Test match at Trent Bridge in 2018
sports.nri_angle: The Bay Area's Indian diaspora finally has a cricket icon playing competitive matches in their backyard — Ashwin's MLC debut connects millions of NRIs to the sport on American soil.

technology.title: India's First Private Rocket Is Headed to the Launchpad. The Window Opens July 12.
technology.excerpt: Skyroot Aerospace, founded by two ex-ISRO engineers and now valued at $1.1 billion, will attempt to put a satellite in orbit from Sriharikota — a milestone no Indian private company has reached.
technology.image_caption: Skyroot's Vikram-S rocket launching during Mission Prarambh from Sriharikota in 2022
technology.nri_angle: NRI investors and Indian-American tech leaders like Alphabet board member Ram Shriram are backing India's private space race, which aims to build a $44 billion economy by 2033.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: India and Japan Just Signed an AI Pact. Their First Target Is a Joint Language Model.
technology.excerpt: At their 16th annual summit in New Delhi, Modi and Takaichi inked agreements on AI, semiconductors, and critical minerals — positioning both countries to reduce their dependence on American and Chinese tech stacks.
technology.image_caption: Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi, who visited New Delhi for the 16th India-Japan annual summit
technology.nri_angle: Indian-origin engineers at Japanese firms and NRI researchers at IITs stand to gain from the AI research partnership, while semiconductor collaboration opens new career and investment pathways beyond Silicon Valley.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Every Big Tech Company Is Building Data Centres in India. The Tax Break Lasts Until 2047.
technology.excerpt: Microsoft, Google, Amazon, Meta, and OpenAI have collectively committed over $80 billion to Indian data centre infrastructure. Nomura says capacity will grow tenfold in a decade.
technology.image_caption: Server racks with fibre optic cables inside a modern data centre
technology.nri_angle: NRI engineers at FAANG companies are building the very AI infrastructure being deployed to India, while the data centre boom creates investment, career, and return-to-India opportunities across cloud, networking, and power engineering.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Nadella, Pichai and Arora Just Bought a Cricket Team at Lord's. The Price Tag Was £145 Million.
technology.excerpt: A consortium of 11 Indian-origin Silicon Valley executives outbid IPL moguls to acquire a 49% stake in London Spirit — the franchise that plays at the most storied ground in cricket.
technology.image_caption: Nikesh Arora, CEO of Palo Alto Networks, who led the consortium of Indian-origin tech CEOs
technology.nri_angle: The deal shows how deeply Indian-origin tech wealth is reshaping global sport ownership — from MLC in the US to The Hundred in England — and signals a new route for diaspora capital into cricket's commercial backbone.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Microsoft Is Building a 3,600-Km Undersea Cable From India to Singapore. Tata Communications Is Helping.
technology.excerpt: The I-2SEA cable consortium — which also includes Singtel and Japan's NEC — will land in the same Indian port city where Meta and Google are building data centers. It could be operational by late 2029.
technology.image_caption: Aerial view of Microsoft's West Campus in Redmond, Washington — the tech giant is now building a 3,600-km undersea cable from India to Singapore
technology.nri_angle: The undersea cable and the $80 billion data center buildout behind it are creating a massive new demand center for Indian engineering talent — and making India-origin cloud services viable at a scale that could eventually rival the US for NRI-run enterprises.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: UPI Now Processes 757 Million Transactions a Day. Greece Just Became Its 10th Country.
technology.excerpt: India's digital payments juggernaut hit a new daily record in June even as monthly volumes pulled back from May's all-time high. Meanwhile, SBI-backed Cashfree is betting on cross-border travel and investment payments.
technology.image_caption: India's UPI digital payment system, built by the National Payments Corporation of India, now live in 10 countries including Greece
technology.nri_angle: For the millions of NRIs who send money home, shop on Indian e-commerce platforms, or invest in Indian markets, UPI's international expansion and the fintech cross-border push directly reduce the friction and cost of staying financially connected to India.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: JP Morgan Says AI Is Deflating India's IT Giants. It Picked Two Winners.
technology.excerpt: The brokerage expects only 3-4% growth for Indian IT services as AI compresses delivery timelines. TCS and Infosys are favoured; HCLTech and Wipro are not.
technology.image_caption: Aerial view of the glass pyramid at the Infosys campus in Mysore, India
technology.nri_angle: Hundreds of thousands of NRIs work at Indian IT firms or hold their stocks — this downgrade signals structural change in the industry that built the diaspora's professional class.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: OpenAI's First Hardware Is a Macro Pad for Coders. It Launches July 15.
technology.excerpt: The Codex Micro, built with keyboard maker Work Louder, gives developers physical buttons for AI-assisted coding shortcuts. It is not the Jony Ive device.
technology.image_caption: Sam Altman, CEO of OpenAI, which is launching its first hardware product on July 15 (Wikimedia Commons)
technology.nri_angle: India has the world's second-largest developer community and OpenAI just hired ex-Uber India chief Prabhjeet Singh as its India MD — this hardware play signals growing investment in the developer ecosystem Indian engineers dominate.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Indian Tech Workers Are Self-Sponsoring Their Green Cards. EB-1A Filings Have Jumped 50%.
technology.excerpt: With H-1B costs soaring and layoffs triggering 60-day exit clocks, senior Indian engineers are bypassing employer-sponsored immigration entirely. The EB-1A 'extraordinary ability' visa is their escape hatch.
technology.image_caption: H-1B visa application documents at the US Citizenship and Immigration Services
technology.nri_angle: EB-1A self-petitions directly affect tens of thousands of Indian H-1B professionals in the US — this is the immigration strategy shift of a generation for the tech diaspora.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Apple Tells India Its Antitrust Case Was 'Copy-Pasted.' The Fine Could Hit $38 Billion.
technology.excerpt: In its sharpest legal filing yet, Apple accuses the CCI of recycling rivals' complaints rather than conducting independent analysis — but India's regulators have heard that argument before, from Google.
technology.image_caption: Aerial view of Apple Park in Cupertino, California — headquarters of a company now facing up to $38 billion in antitrust exposure in India
technology.nri_angle: Indian-origin iOS developers and fintech founders on both sides of the Pacific could see fundamental changes to how the App Store operates in India, while PhonePe — widely used by NRIs for cross-border payments — is among the complainants.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: India Is Building 20 AI Models to Rival ChatGPT. Its Strategy Is to Skip the Arms Race.
technology.excerpt: As the US restricts its most powerful AI systems, India is funding homegrown open-source models that deliver 60-80% of frontier capability — and betting that's enough for most of the world.
technology.image_caption: India's Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology is driving the country's sovereign AI push, including 20 indigenous large language models
technology.nri_angle: Indian-origin AI researchers at Google, OpenAI, and Anthropic now have open-source Indian models to build on, while NRI investors get exposure to a government-backed AI ecosystem producing tangible outputs.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Companies Spending the Most on AI Are Hiring the Fastest. The Full Story Is More Complicated.
technology.excerpt: A new study of 22,000 companies finds heavy AI adopters grew headcount 10%. But 185,000 tech workers lost jobs this year, and Indians on H-1B are the most exposed population of all.
technology.image_caption: An illustration of artificial intelligence and machine learning — the technology reshaping both hiring and layoff patterns across Silicon Valley
technology.nri_angle: Indians hold the largest share of H-1B visas and are disproportionately affected by AI-driven layoffs, while senior Indian engineers are increasingly pursuing EB-1A green cards to decouple their immigration status from volatile employers.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: Turmeric's Active Compound Can Ease Depression as Effectively as Some Drugs — and the Evidence Is Growing
lifestyle-health.excerpt: A meta-analysis presented at the APA 2026 meeting found curcumin supplements produced a 'moderate-to-large' reduction in depressive symptoms across five randomised trials — with zero major side effects reported
lifestyle-health.image_caption: Turmeric root and curcumin powder, the golden spice now backed by clinical evidence for depression treatment
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: Turmeric is the signature spice of Indian kitchens and Ayurveda — this clinical evidence validates ancestral knowledge and gives diaspora families a culturally familiar tool to discuss mental health.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: Living in a Walkable Neighbourhood Could Be as Important for Your Health as Diet or Exercise, a Major New Study Finds
lifestyle-health.excerpt: An MIT-led analysis of 28,000 U.S. census tracts, published in Nature Health, found that urban design — green spaces, mixed-use streets, and short connected blocks — is a powerful and independent predictor of both physical and mental health outcomes
lifestyle-health.image_caption: Central Park in New York City — walkable green spaces are linked to better physical and mental health outcomes
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: For NRIs choosing between US cities and suburbs, this study offers data-backed guidance: walkable, green neighborhoods don't just feel better — they measurably protect your physical and mental health.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: Millennials and Gen X Are Aging Faster Biologically Than Their Parents — and a Major Study Links It to Rising Cancer Rates
lifestyle-health.excerpt: A Nature Medicine analysis of over 150,000 people finds that recent generations show accelerated biological aging, which may help explain the surge in early-onset cancers — a trend with particular implications for South Asians.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: Biological aging research: Chemical laboratory at the central cancer research labs
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: South Asians already face elevated metabolic and cancer risks at younger ages; accelerated biological aging in recent generations adds a compounding vulnerability that standard screening timelines may not account for.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: Nestlé Will Strip Artificial Colourings From Every Product on Earth by Year-End — and It Could Reshape What Indians Eat
lifestyle-health.excerpt: The Swiss food giant becomes the first major packaged-food company to set a global deadline for eliminating synthetic dyes, a move driven by GLP-1 drug pressure and RFK Jr.'s FDA crackdown that could ripple through Maggi, KitKat, and Munch in India
lifestyle-health.image_caption: Nestlé products in a retail store — the company plans to remove all artificial colourings from its global portfolio by end-2026
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: NRIs navigating different food safety standards between the US/UK and India may finally see consistency as Nestlé standardises its ingredient lists globally — including for iconic Indian brands like Maggi and KitKat
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: A Simultaneous Heat Emergency Is Scorching Two Continents — and Millions of Indian Diaspora Are in Its Path
lifestyle-health.excerpt: Europe's deadliest heatwave in years has killed over 1,300 people, and now a punishing heat dome is descending on the US for July 4th. For the 7 million-strong Indian diaspora across both regions, the message is the same: this is not normal summer heat.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: Extreme heat conditions — a simultaneous heatwave is affecting both the United States and South Asia (Wikimedia Commons)
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: Over 6 million Indian-origin residents in the US and UK face record-breaking heat in their home cities, with multigenerational households and elderly family members at acute risk.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: A New Weight-Loss Drug Just Matched Bariatric Surgery — and It Could Change How South Asians Fight Obesity
lifestyle-health.excerpt: Eli Lilly's retatrutide produced 28% weight loss at 80 weeks in the landmark TRIUMPH-1 trial, the first medication ever to rival surgical outcomes — a potential game-changer for a community with the world's highest metabolic disease burden.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: An Ozempic injection pen — retatrutide belongs to the same GLP-1 drug class but targets three metabolic receptors instead of one
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: South Asians carry the world's highest metabolic disease burden relative to BMI — a drug matching bariatric surgery outcomes could transform obesity treatment for the diaspora.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: The Weedkiller in Your Food May Be Rewiring Your Brain Through Your Gut — and the 'Safe' Doses Aren't So Safe
lifestyle-health.excerpt: A wave of new research finds glyphosate — sprayed on wheat, oats, lentils, and most American crops — disrupts gut bacteria, alters brain chemistry, and triggers anxiety-like behavior at doses far below regulatory limits
lifestyle-health.image_caption: Agricultural spraying in a crop field — glyphosate is the world's most widely used herbicide
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: NRIs face high glyphosate exposure through the American food supply — and India's own use of the herbicide on tea, wheat, and lentils means the risk cuts across both food systems
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: Medicare Will Now Cover Ozempic and Wegovy for Weight Loss — Here's Who Qualifies and What It Costs
lifestyle-health.excerpt: A new pilot program launching July 1 lets eligible seniors get GLP-1 drugs for just $50 a month, but the fine print matters — and the clock is already ticking.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: An Ozempic (semaglutide) injection pen — Medicare will now cover GLP-1 medications for weight loss (Wikimedia Commons)
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: South Asians face elevated metabolic risk at lower BMI thresholds, and many NRI families are navigating Medicare coverage for aging parents — making this program particularly relevant for multigenerational Indian American households.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: South Asians Have the Highest Heart Disease Risk at 45 — Despite Eating Better and Drinking Less Than Everyone Else
lifestyle-health.excerpt: A decade-long study of 2,700 U.S. adults found that South Asian men and women develop prediabetes, hypertension, and high cholesterol earlier than every other racial group — even though they report healthier diets and lower alcohol use. The researchers say visceral fat and early-life exposures may explain the paradox.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: A doctor checks blood pressure during a cardiovascular screening — researchers say South Asians should begin heart health screenings before midlife
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: South Asian Americans face the highest cardiovascular risk of any U.S. racial group by age 45 — a finding that demands earlier screening, lipoprotein(a) testing, and culturally tailored care for the diaspora community.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: Walking 10,000 Steps a Day Can Offset a Full Day at Your Desk, a 72,000-Person Study Finds
lifestyle-health.excerpt: Researchers at the University of Sydney found that each increase in daily steps — up to about 10,000 — was linked to a 39% lower risk of death and 21% lower risk of heart disease, regardless of how many hours participants spent sitting. For the millions of South Asian tech workers who log 8-plus hours at a desk, the data offers a clear prescription.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: Walking remains the most accessible countermeasure to prolonged sitting, with benefits scaling up to about 10,000 steps per day
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: South Asian tech workers in the U.S. spend 8-10 hours at desks — among the highest sedentary rates of any demographic — and already face elevated cardiovascular risk by midlife. Walking 10,000 steps daily can meaningfully offset the damage.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: Americans Are Ditching Multivitamins for Targeted Supplements — and Two of the Fastest-Growing Are Ayurvedic Staples
lifestyle-health.excerpt: A 25-year JAMA analysis of 63,000 adults finds supplement use surging while multivitamin use drops — with turmeric and ashwagandha leading the charge
lifestyle-health.image_caption: Assorted dietary supplements including vitamin D, magnesium, and turmeric capsules
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: Turmeric and ashwagandha — Ayurvedic staples in South Asian households — are now among America's fastest-growing supplements, while targeted vitamin D matters disproportionately for NRIs at higher latitudes.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: The FDA Just Cleared an AI Tool That Detects Hidden Heart Disease From a Routine ECG — and South Asians May Benefit Most
lifestyle-health.excerpt: EchoNext, trained on 700,000 ECG records, caught severe heart failure a cardiologist missed — and its clearance could reshape screening for high-risk populations
lifestyle-health.image_caption: An electrocardiogram readout showing heart rhythm patterns
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: South Asians face 2-4x higher coronary disease rates and often develop heart disease a decade earlier — an AI tool that reads hidden cardiac risk from routine ECGs could catch disease years before symptoms appear.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

food.title: The Fake Dosa Makers: How AI-Generated Videos Are Weaponising Indian Street Food
food.excerpt: Millions of views, zero reality — AI-generated clips depicting unsanitary Indian food preparation are going viral, and the diaspora is paying the reputational price.
food.image_caption: Sev puri chaat, a real Indian street food dish — vibrant, hygienic, and made with craft
food.nri_angle: AI-generated fake videos depicting unsanitary Indian food preparation are fuelling anti-Indian stereotypes online, undercutting the diaspora's decades-long effort to gain respect for Indian cuisine in the West.
food.author: Diaspora Desk

food.title: The $24 Bag of Rice: How US Tariffs Are Reshaping the Desi Pantry
food.excerpt: With US duties on Indian goods at 50 percent, staples from Sona Masoori rice to filter coffee have surged in price — and Pakistani brands are quietly filling the gap.
food.image_caption: Assorted Indian spices and grains in burlap bags at a grocery store
food.nri_angle: The 50 percent US tariff on Indian goods is directly hitting NRI family budgets, turning everyday pantry staples like rice, dal, and coffee into luxury items.
food.author: Diaspora Desk

food.title: From Pani Puri to Prix Fixe: Sujan Sarkar's Michelin Empire Lands in New York and Phoenix
food.excerpt: The first Bengali chef to earn a Michelin star in America opens two restaurants in five weeks, stretching Indian fine dining from Hudson Yards to the Arizona desert.
food.image_caption: Pani puri served at an Indian restaurant, a dish Sarkar has reimagined as an oyster course
food.nri_angle: Sarkar's expansion from Chicago to New York and Phoenix proves Indian fine dining is now viable beyond coastal food capitals, giving NRIs across America access to world-class Indian cuisine.

food.title: Chicken Stock in Dal Makhani? A Former MasterChef Judge Just Ignited Indian Food's Loudest Fight
food.excerpt: George Calombaris's Instagram reel adding chicken stock cubes to dal makhani has reignited the perennial debate over who gets to reinterpret Indian classics — and where the red line sits.
food.image_caption: A bowl of traditional dal makhani garnished with cream and fresh coriander
food.nri_angle: For NRIs who grew up eating their mother's dal makhani, the controversy touches a nerve about cultural ownership and whether Western chefs dilute Indian food's identity as it goes global.
food.author: Diaspora Desk

food.title: From a Hotel Lobby in Fort Collins to a Strip Mall in Columbus: Indian Food Is Showing Up Everywhere
food.excerpt: A new wave of Indian restaurants is quietly spreading into mid-sized American cities far from the coastal corridors, driven by immigrant families betting on untapped appetites.
food.image_caption: A traditional Indian thali with an assortment of dishes — Indian restaurants are popping up in unexpected American cities from Fort Collins to Columbus
food.nri_angle: For NRIs living outside traditional desi enclaves, these openings signal that Indian food is becoming accessible in the kinds of cities where finding a decent biryani once meant a two-hour drive.

food.title: Tandoori on the Grill: How the Desi Fourth of July Became a Diaspora Tradition
food.excerpt: This Independence Day, Indian Americans are bringing tikka marinades, masala corn, and chutney sliders to the backyard cookout — reshaping what the all-American BBQ looks like
food.image_caption: Tandoori chicken on the grill — a scene increasingly common at Indian American Fourth of July cookouts

food.title: The Beard's New Palate: Indian Cuisine's Record Run at America's Most Prestigious Food Awards
food.excerpt: From Chai Pani to Tamba to Cal-India Collective, a record number of South Asian finalists at the 2026 James Beard Awards signals a seismic shift in how America eats
food.image_caption: The James Beard Foundation Award medallion — this year, Indian and South Asian chefs competed for it in unprecedented numbers

food.title: Vacuum-Sealed Nostalgia: The Gujarati Home Kitchens Feeding America's NRIs
food.excerpt: In Mumbai and Ahmedabad, a network of women entrepreneurs is vacuum-packing thepla, khakhra, and fafda for suitcase-bound NRIs — and the business is booming
food.image_caption: A traditional Gujarati snack spread — the kind of comfort food that travels thousands of miles in vacuum-sealed packages to NRI doorsteps

food.title: The Quiet Grocery Conquest: Inside Patel Brothers' Push Into America's Fastest-Growing Suburbs
food.excerpt: From a single Chicago storefront in 1974 to over 50 locations nationwide, the largest Indian grocery chain in America is following the diaspora into suburbs that never had a dal section — and reshaping what neighbourhood grocery stores look like.
food.image_caption: Devon Avenue in Chicago, home to the original Patel Brothers store and one of America's densest concentrations of South Asian commerce (Wikimedia Commons)
food.nri_angle: For NRIs who once drove hours for a packet of Haldiram's or fresh curry leaves, a Patel Brothers opening in their suburb means home has come to them.
food.author: Diaspora Desk

food.title: Tikka Masala Naan, Bombay Spice Chips, and Beet Tikka Patties: Indian Food Just Swept America's Top Grocery Awards
food.excerpt: Three Indian-inspired brands earned top honours at the 2026 NEXTY Awards — the natural food industry's equivalent of the Oscars — in a year that confirmed Indian cuisine's breakout moment in American retail.
food.image_caption: Freshly baked butter naan served alongside three different Indian curries
food.nri_angle: For NRIs who have spent years explaining what naan is to American colleagues, watching Indian food win mainstream grocery awards feels like vindication — and a sign that the frozen aisle is finally catching up to their kitchens.
food.author: Diaspora Desk

food.title: The Air Fryer Rewrote the Samosa: How NRI Kitchens Became 2026's Viral Recipe Labs
food.excerpt: From oil-free samosas racking up 15 million views to jaggery rasmalai tres leches cakes that fuse two continents in a single dessert, the most viral Indian recipes of 2026 are being invented in diaspora kitchens.
food.image_caption: Golden, crispy samosas served as a popular Indian snack
food.nri_angle: NRI kitchens — caught between their mothers' recipes and American appliance culture — have become the unlikely laboratories for the most inventive Indian food content on the internet.
food.author: Diaspora Desk

food.title: Musaafer's Taj Mahal Comes to Tribeca: Inside New York's Most Opulent Indian Restaurant
food.excerpt: The Houston fine-dining sensation — where lotus chandeliers hang above nihari birria tacos and butter chicken arrives as a two-act experience — opens a lavish second act in lower Manhattan.
food.image_caption: The Tribeca neighbourhood in Manhattan, where Musaafer has opened New York's most opulent Indian restaurant (Wikimedia Commons)
food.nri_angle: For Indian Americans tired of explaining that their food culture extends far beyond chicken tikka masala, Musaafer's state-by-state culinary journey is a showcase of India's staggering diversity.

carousel.title: The Ram Mandir Donation Scandal Has Reached ₹200 Crore. Eight Are in Jail. Fifty More Are Under the Scanner.
carousel.excerpt: CCTV caught temple staff skimming cash from donation boxes. Investigators found a 70-room hostel, luxury cars, and a paper trail that may stretch far beyond the eight arrests.
carousel.image_caption: The Ram Mandir in Ayodhya during its inauguration ceremony in January 2024
carousel.nri_angle: Millions of NRIs donated to the Ram Mandir construction fund, and the embezzlement scandal directly undermines the trust diaspora communities placed in the temple administration.

carousel.title: The Director of Vikram Just Picked Up the Gun Himself
carousel.excerpt: Lokesh Kanagaraj makes his acting debut as a gangster Devdas in DC — directed by Arun Matheswaran, scored by Anirudh, trailer-premiered at Cannes. Tamil cinema's busiest man just found a new job.

carousel.title: Gardner and Perry Won't Be Stopped. Australia Crush West Indies to Reach Another Women's T20 World Cup Final.
carousel.excerpt: An eight-wicket demolition at The Oval sends Australia into Sunday's final at Lord's — the same ground where they ended India's campaign four days ago. England or South Africa will be their opponent.
carousel.image_caption: Ellyse Perry, whose half-century against India and consistent performances have powered Australia's run to the Women's T20 World Cup final
carousel.nri_angle: India's second consecutive group-stage exit puts pressure on the Harmanpreet Kaur era, while NRIs in the UK can attend the final at Lord's — but will be watching as neutrals after their team's heartbreak at the same venue.
carousel.author: Diaspora Desk

carousel.title: India and Japan Just Signed an AI Pact. Their First Target Is a Joint Language Model.
carousel.excerpt: At their 16th annual summit in New Delhi, Modi and Takaichi inked agreements on AI, semiconductors, and critical minerals — positioning both countries to reduce their dependence on American and Chinese tech stacks.
carousel.image_caption: Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi, who visited New Delhi for the 16th India-Japan annual summit
carousel.nri_angle: Indian-origin engineers at Japanese firms and NRI researchers at IITs stand to gain from the AI research partnership, while semiconductor collaboration opens new career and investment pathways beyond Silicon Valley.
carousel.author: Diaspora Desk

carousel.title: India Is About to Witness Its Biggest-Ever IPO Wave — From Jio's $3.8 Billion Listing to Carlsberg's Beer Play
carousel.excerpt: Carlsberg has confidentially filed for a $700 million India IPO, joining a pipeline that includes Jio Platforms, NSE, PhonePe, and Pernod Ricard — collectively the largest collection of marquee listings India has ever seen in a single year
carousel.image_caption: The National Stock Exchange of India, set to host what could be the country's biggest IPO wave
carousel.nri_angle: NRI investors who can access Indian IPOs through demat accounts or GIFT City–routed platforms face a once-in-a-generation lineup — but the sheer volume of issuance will test whether the market can absorb it all.
